scope: Make the synthetic Google owner-verification ciphertext tamper test guaranteed to modify authentication bytes; preserve blocked Starter activation evidence
riskAnalysis: Test-only correction; production encryption and authorization unchanged. A fixed Base64URL suffix could already equal the existing random suffix, so the negative fixture sometimes supplied valid unchanged ciphertext. Decode, flip GCM tag byte12, re-encode and assert wire/byte inequality before expecting denial. The actual failed build packet was not retained and must not be reconstructed by assertion.

defects.rootCause: The synthetic tamper fixture replaced a random suffix with AA without asserting that any bytes changed; a deterministic valid packet demonstrated an exact no-op.
defects.detectionGap: Previous randomly generated fixture packets normally differed at this suffix, allowing the unasserted no-op case to escape repeated passing runs.
defects.regression: Guarantee a changed authentication tag and assert both encoded and decoded inequality while retaining ownerCredentialVerified=false denial; independent Google focused77 and Auditor12 checks pass.
defects.historicalPrevention: Negative authentication fixtures should mutate decoded authenticated bytes and assert mutation occurred instead of relying on random wire suffix differences. Preserve original failed build and its unknown nonce.
